title: Diagonal scheme tests of a monomorphism into a base change
statement:
Let $S,T,B$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $T,B$ over $S$, and let $b:B\to T$ be an $S$-morphism. Let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], let $f:X\to h_T$ be a morphism, and put $X_B=X\times_{h_T}h_B$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $j:Y\to X_B$ be injective on sections over every $S$-scheme (a monomorphism of sheaves). Let $g:Y\to h_B$ and $r:Y\to X$ be the two composites. For every $S$-scheme $D$ and morphism $d:h_D\to Y\times_{h_B}Y$, let $y_1,y_2\in Y(D)$ be its components, with common image $\beta\in h_B(D)$, and let $x_i=r(y_i)$. There is a canonical isomorphism over $h_D$
$$h_D\times_{Y\times_{h_B}Y}Y\ \cong\ h_D\times_{X\times_{h_T}X}X,$$
where both maps from $Y$ and $X$ are the relative diagonals and the map on the right from $h_D$ is $(x_1,x_2)$. The isomorphism is natural in further scheme tests over $D$. In particular, if every scheme test of $\Delta_{X/T}$ is represented by a scheme closed-immersed in its test scheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], the same holds for $\Delta_{Y/B}$. The assertion includes $Y=X_B$, $j=1_{X_B}$. Sheaf fibre products are computed as compatible pairs of sections as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], and scheme fibre products use [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), proof diagonal pullback formula; Tag 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated), specialized to a monomorphism, with equality-locus scheme tests.

proof.text: Write $L=h_D\times_{Y\times_{h_B}Y}Y$ and $R=h_D\times_{X\times_{h_T}X}X$. For an $S$-scheme $E$ and $u:E\to D$, naturality gives $d_E(u)=(y_1|_u,y_2|_u)$ by evaluating $d_D$ at $1_D$. In particular $g(y_i|_u)=\beta|_u$ and $f(x_i|_u)=b\beta|_u$. By the compatible-pair convention in the statement, $L(E)$ consists of $(u,y)$ with $y=y_1|_u=y_2|_u$; $R(E)$ consists of $(u,x)$ with $x=x_1|_u=x_2|_u$. Here natural transformations and representable functors have the meanings in [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), diagonal base-change formula; Tag 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated), diagonal factorization, with the monomorphism case checked on sections.

proof.text: The pair description of $X_B(E)$ gives $j_E(y_i|_u)=(x_i|_u,\beta|_u)$. Hence $x_1|_u=x_2|_u$ implies equality of these pairs, and injectivity of $j_E$ implies $y_1|_u=y_2|_u$. Conversely applying $r_E$ to this last equality gives $x_1|_u=x_2|_u$. Only the assumed injectivity on sections is used; $r_E$ itself need not be injective.

source.place: Tag 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), diagonal base-change formula; Tag 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated), diagonal factorization, with the monomorphism case checked on sections.

proof.text: Define $\Phi_E:L(E)\to R(E)$ by $(u,y)\mapsto(u,r_E(y))$. Define $\Psi_E:R(E)\to L(E)$ by $(u,x)\mapsto(u,y_1|_u)$, which is well-defined by step 2. Their composites are identities: in $L(E)$ one already has $y=y_1|_u$, and in $R(E)$ one has $x=x_1|_u=r_E(y_1|_u)$. For $v:E'\to E$, restriction replaces $u$ by $uv$ and $y_1|_u$ by $y_1|_{uv}$; naturality of $r$ shows both formulas commute with restriction. Thus these are inverse sheaf morphisms over $h_D$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Replacing $D$ by any $D'\to D$ gives the very same formulas, proving the claimed naturality in further scheme tests.

source.place: Tag 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), diagonal base-change formula; Tag 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated), diagonal factorization, with the monomorphism case checked on sections.

proof.text: Under the closed-diagonal-test hypothesis, choose a representation $h_Z\cong R$ over $h_D$ with $Z\to D$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Compose it with $\Psi$ to obtain $h_Z\cong L$ over $h_D$, in the sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The representing scheme and its projection $Z\to D$ are exactly the same, so this is the required closed-immersion test for $\Delta_{Y/B}$. This applies to every $D,d$. Finally $j=1_{X_B}$ is injective on sections, so the same argument includes $Y=X_B$.

L and R are the subfunctors {u: y_1|_u=y_2|_u} and {u: x_1|_u=x_2|_u} of h_D. Because j(y_i|_u)=(x_i|_u,β|_u) has the same second component for i=1,2, injectivity of j gives L=R. The closed-immersion consequence then reuses the same Z→D. Monicity of j and the common B-component are both necessary, and the proof uses both. Steps: 1 is the Yoneda computation by hand plus the pair descriptions, using def-trf-algebraic-space. 2 uses only injectivity of j. 3 gives Φ and Ψ, shows they are inverse, and checks naturality under restriction and under D'→D. 4 transports the representation by h_Z, using def-weil-closed-immersion. The steps use definitions only, so no tool_uses are needed, and proof_deps equals the union of the uses. Edge cases checked: j=id (which parent step 3 uses), empty Y, empty D, y_1=y_2, sections that become equal only after restriction, and X=h_T with r=b not monic. lean.statement: theorem space_monic_diagonal_tests {S : Scheme.{u}} (T B : Over S) (b : B ⟶ T) (X Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (j : Y.obj.obj ⟶ Limits.pullback f (yoneda.map b)) (hj : ∀ E : Over S, Function.Injective (j.app (op E))) : (∀ (D : Over S) (d : yoneda.obj D ⟶ Limits.pullback (j ≫ pullback.snd f (yoneda.map b)) (j ≫ pullback.snd f (yoneda.map b))), IsIso (monicDiagonalTestMap f b j d) ∧ monicDiagonalTestMap f b j d ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = pullback.fst _ _ ∧ ∀ (D' : Over S) (v : D' ⟶ D), diagonalTestRestriction (pullback.diagonal (j ≫ pullback.snd f (yoneda.map b))) d v ≫ monicDiagonalTestMap f b j d = monicDiagonalTestMap f b j (yoneda.map v ≫ d) ≫ diagonalTestRestriction (pullback.diagonal f) (d ≫ monicDiagonalPairMap f b j) v) ∧ (IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (pullback.diagonal f) → IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (pullback.diagonal (j ≫ pullback.snd f (yoneda.map b))))
lean.note: The canonical comparison is constructed by pullback.map with the identity test component and r on the space component. The theorem asserts its invertibility, its equation over the test scheme, naturality under further tests, and the closed-immersion-test consequence. The three helper maps contain real data and only structural commutativity proofs.
